thread:
alex: FYI escalation — customer reported a sudden latency spike and a big cross-region egress bill. They say most traffic routed to eu-west even though policy should favor us-west. Customer is sensitive to latency.
ops-bot: [ALERT] cust-568: cross-region egress > 3x baseline (us-west -> eu-west). Top URI: /v1/generate
alex: Repro notes from support: 2026-03-09 15:12-15:30 UTC. Error rates OK, but p95 latency jumped from 120ms -> 540ms for a subset of their requests. Billing shows egress increase to eu-west. Asked customer for failover policy; they pasted below.
alex: ```json
{
  "failover_policy": {
    "mode": "weighted",
    "sticky": true,
    "regions": ["us-west-2","eu-west-1"],
    "weights": [0.9, 0.1]
  }
}
```
maria: :eyes: thanks. Quick Qs: did they create weights as decimals? Our routing config historically expected integer weights. Can you paste the raw config from the API (not the UI)? Also need a sample request id that hit eu-west.
alex: pasted raw config from their tenant record (same as above). Sample request id that hit eu-west: req_20260309_8f3a. Raw routing decision log for that request:

```
[2026-03-09T15:14:02Z] tenant=cust-568 req=req_20260309_8f3a routed_region=eu-west-1 policy_mode=weighted computed_weights=[0,0] selected_region=eu-west-1
```
liam: Ok this is interesting. Looks like the parser truncated the decimal weights to ints, turning 0.9 -> 0 and 0.1 -> 0. When all weights are 0 we fall back to priority enumeration (which for this tenant is eu-west first due to legacy ordering), and sticky/session affinity was effectively bypassed. I've not seen decimal weights in customer-provided configs before. :thinking_face:
nora: Confirming: our validator on the UI coerces percentages to integers (90/10) but the raw API accepts JSON and the runtime parser does an int cast without validating range/format. Edge case: customers who used fractional weights (0.9 style) end up with zeros.
maria: That explains cross-region. Can we reproduce locally and make a short mitigation? If we can detect non-integer weights at runtime and reject with a 400, that would immediately prevent future escapes.
liam: Repro steps I ran locally:
1) `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/tenant/cust-568/routing -d '{"failover_policy": {"mode":"weighted","sticky":true,"regions":["us-west-2","eu-west-1"],"weights":[0.9,0.1]}}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'`
2) Send a sample request: `curl -H 'X-Tenant: cust-568' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -d '{...}'`
3) Check router debug: `/internal/debug/routing?req=req_...` log shows computed_weights `[0,0]` and routing to eu-west per priority.
liam: Patch idea: change parser to accept floats and normalize by sum -> integers for internal table OR validate and reject non-integers with helpful error. I'll open a hotfix PR to validate and reject decimals so we can push a config-safe guard quickly.
maria: For immediate mitigation we rolled back the tenant policy to a safe integer-based one on their behalf: `weights: [90,10]` (via support backend write). Customer confirmed latency returned to normal within 2 minutes.
alex: Customer update: "Thanks, support — looks fixed after you changed weights. Can you explain why decimals broke routing so we can avoid this?" We offered a short postmortem.
liam: I'll send a quick hotfix: validate on ingestion (API) and add a warning in Console if UI sends decimals. Longer term: extend parser to accept floats and normalize. Risk of normalization change for existing code paths, so do validator first.
nora: Also adding a regression test in routing unit tests for fractional weights -> ensure either reject or correctly normalize. Filing ENG-PRIORITY ticket.
ops-bot: [DEPLOY] support/roll-forward 1.2.3 -> rolled back tenant config for cust-568 by alex @ 2026-03-09T15:22:41Z
alex: Closing loop: Customer notified, billing team alerted to investigate the egress spike refund/credit. Scheduling a short customer-facing note once patch is in. Follow-ups: ENG to open PR (liam), SRE to add anomaly alert rule for computed_weights all-zero (maria), Support to check for other tenants with decimal weights and auto-correct if safe (alex). :white_check_mark:
